title: Design a Food Delivery App (DoorDash) — Object Model
prompt: Design the object model for a food delivery platform like DoorDash or Uber Eats. Customers browse restaurants and menus, build a cart, place an order, and the order flows from placed → confirmed → preparing → picked up → delivered. Design the core classes, the cart and order model, the order state machine, and pricing/promotions. Focus on class design and APIs rather than the distributed backend. Sketch the class diagram.
blurb: Restaurant/menu modeling, a cart-to-order flow, an order state machine spanning three actors, and pluggable pricing/promos.

rubric.label: Requirements clarification
rubric.description: Separates functional (browse, cart, order, three-party lifecycle, payment, delivery tracking) from non-functional (menu-price consistency, order correctness, extensible promos).

rubric.label: Core entities
rubric.description: Customer, Restaurant, MenuItem, Cart, CartItem, Order, OrderItem, DeliveryAgent, Payment, Promotion — cleanly separated.

rubric.label: Class design & responsibilities
rubric.description: Cart vs Order separation; OrderItem snapshots price at order time; pricing/promotions are their own components.

rubric.label: Relationships & cardinality
rubric.description: Restaurant 1..* MenuItem; Cart 1..* CartItem; Order 1..* OrderItem; Order references one Customer, one Restaurant, one DeliveryAgent. Composition vs association reasoned.

rubric.label: Design patterns
rubric.description: State for order lifecycle, Strategy for pricing/promotions and delivery-agent assignment, Builder for Cart→Order, Observer for status notifications, Decorator for item add-ons/customizations.

rubric.label: SOLID / OCP
rubric.description: New promo type or delivery-fee rule plugs in without editing Order; item customization via composition; state logic localized.

rubric.label: API / method design
rubric.description: addToCart, checkout, placeOrder, confirmOrder, assignAgent, updateStatus, applyPromo — clear ownership.

rubric.label: Order state machine
rubric.description: Explicit states + legal transitions across customer/restaurant/agent; cancellation/refund from valid states.

rubric.label: Edge cases
rubric.description: Item out of stock at checkout, restaurant offline, price changed after add-to-cart, promo not applicable, no agents, partial cancellation.

rubric.label: Concurrency
rubric.description: Inventory/availability at checkout, double order submission, agent double-assignment, price snapshot vs live menu.

rubric.label: Extensibility
rubric.description: Group orders, scheduled orders, new promo types, multi-restaurant carts, tips, ratings added cleanly.

rubric.label: Communication
rubric.description: Narrates cart→order flow and state diagram, states tradeoffs, reasons about price snapshotting.

functional_requirements: Browse restaurants and their menus (items, prices, availability, customizations)
Build a cart from one restaurant; adjust quantities and add-ons
Checkout: apply promos, compute item total + tax + delivery fee + tip, pay
Place order; order flows PLACED → CONFIRMED → PREPARING → READY → PICKED_UP → DELIVERED
Assign a delivery agent; track status; notify customer
Cancel/refund within allowed states; rate restaurant and agent
nonfunctional_requirements: Order captures the price at checkout time even if the menu later changes
Order correctness — totals reconcile (items + tax + fee + tip − discount)
Extensible promotions, delivery-fee rules, and assignment policies
A single order handled by exactly one delivery agent
clarifying_questions: Single-restaurant carts only, or multi-restaurant / group orders?
What promo types must we support — percent off, flat, free delivery, BOGO?
Is delivery fee flat, distance-based, or surge-based?
Do we schedule future orders or on-demand only?
Who can cancel and from which states — is there a refund policy?

core_classes.name: Restaurant
core_classes.responsibility: Seller with a menu and availability.

core_classes.name: Menu / MenuItem
core_classes.responsibility: Catalog of items; MenuItem holds name, price, availability, and allowed customizations.

core_classes.name: Cart / CartItem
core_classes.responsibility: Mutable pre-order selection tied to one restaurant; CartItem = item + qty + chosen add-ons.

core_classes.name: Order / OrderItem
core_classes.responsibility: Immutable record of a placed cart; OrderItem snapshots name+price at order time.

core_classes.name: OrderState
core_classes.responsibility: State pattern base; each concrete state defines legal transitions and guards.

core_classes.name: PricingEngine
core_classes.responsibility: Computes the Bill: subtotal, tax, delivery fee, tip, minus promotions.

core_classes.name: Promotion
core_classes.responsibility: Abstract discount rule (percent, flat, free-delivery, BOGO) with applicability check.

core_classes.name: AssignmentStrategy
core_classes.responsibility: Abstract: choose a delivery agent for an order.

core_classes.name: OrderService
core_classes.responsibility: Orchestrates checkout → order → lifecycle; coordinates payment, assignment, notifications.

relationships: Restaurant composes a Menu of MenuItems; MenuItem composes allowed AddOns.
Cart is tied to exactly one Restaurant and composes CartItems (each referencing a MenuItem + chosen AddOns).
Order composes OrderItems (price-snapshotted), references one Customer, one Restaurant, one DeliveryAgent, and composes a Bill and OrderState.
PricingEngine depends on DeliveryFeeStrategy, TaxPolicy, and Promotion abstractions (DIP/OCP).
OrderService depends on abstractions: PricingEngine, AssignmentStrategy, PaymentGateway.

design_patterns.where: OrderState subclasses drive the order lifecycle
design_patterns.why: Legal transitions/guards spanning customer, restaurant, and agent live in state objects, not one big switch.
Promo math, fee rules, and courier selection each vary independently and plug in without editing Order/PricingEngine (OCP).

design_patterns.where: Item customizations / add-ons wrap a MenuItem to adjust price
design_patterns.why: Add-ons compose onto items so new customizations don't change the item class.

design_patterns.where: Cart → Order construction (snapshot prices, compute bill, freeze)
design_patterns.why: Assembles a complex immutable Order in a controlled, validated way.

design_patterns.where: Order status changes notify customer/restaurant/agent apps
design_patterns.why: Decouples notification/tracking from core state transitions.

state_transitions: PLACED → CONFIRMED (restaurant accepts) | CANCELLED (restaurant rejects / customer cancels / payment fails)
CANCELLED reachable from PLACED/CONFIRMED (and PREPARING per policy, with refund rules); DELIVERED and CANCELLED terminal
Guards: can't pick up before READY; can't deliver before picked up
edge_cases: Item goes out of stock between add-to-cart and checkout → reprice/remove and warn
Menu price changed after add-to-cart → Order snapshots the price shown at checkout; reconcile if stale
Restaurant offline at checkout → block order
Promo not applicable (min basket, expired, wrong restaurant) → reject with reason
No delivery agents available → queue / delay / notify
Duplicate placeOrder from a retry → idempotency key
Partial cancellation of some items → refund math
Restaurant rejects after payment captured → auto-refund
concurrency: Availability check + order placement should be consistent (avoid selling a just-sold-out item)
assignAgent must atomically flip agent status so one agent isn't double-assigned
Idempotent placeOrder via client requestId to survive retries
Price snapshot at checkout decouples the immutable Order from concurrent menu edits
extensibility: Group orders → a shared Cart with multiple contributors
Scheduled orders → Scheduler submits at time T
New promo types (BOGO, tiered) → new Promotion subclass
Multi-restaurant orders → Order composes sub-orders per restaurant with independent lifecycles
Tips, ratings, reorders → additive without reshaping the core model

deep_dives.probe: Why separate Cart and Order? What does OrderItem store that CartItem doesn't, and why does price snapshotting matter when the menu changes after checkout?
Three actors drive the lifecycle — customer, restaurant, agent. Draw the states and legal transitions. Where does 'can't deliver before pickup' get enforced?
Model percent-off, flat, free-delivery, and BOGO promos so adding a new one doesn't touch PricingEngine. How do stacked promos and applicability checks compose?
'Large, extra cheese, no onions' with price deltas — how do you model item customizations without exploding MenuItem into subclasses?
How is a delivery agent chosen and assigned atomically so no two orders grab the same agent?

followup_bank.question: If the restaurant raises a price after the customer added the item, what price does the order charge? Where is that captured?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions promo or discount or coupon
followup_bank.question: Add a BOGO promo without editing PricingEngine. How do promos declare applicability and stack?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions status or state or lifecycle
followup_bank.question: Who is allowed to move the order from READY to PICKED_UP, and how do you stop an out-of-order transition?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions customization or add-on or topping
followup_bank.question: Model add-ons that change price without subclassing MenuItem for every combination.

followup_bank.trigger: mentions agent or courier or driver
followup_bank.question: How do you assign exactly one agent per order under concurrent assignment?

tradeoffs: Snapshot prices in Order (correctness, storage) vs reference live menu (stale, cheaper)
State pattern (localized transitions, more classes) vs status enum + switch (fewer classes, brittle)
Decorator add-ons (flexible) vs fixed customization fields (simple, rigid)
Single order per restaurant (simple lifecycle) vs multi-restaurant order (better UX, complex per-vendor state)
reference.reference_answer: A strong answer cleanly separates the mutable Cart from the immutable Order, snapshots item prices into OrderItem at checkout so later menu edits don't change a placed order, and models the lifecycle as a State machine spanning customer/restaurant/agent with explicit guards. Pricing is a PricingEngine composing Strategy objects — Promotion, DeliveryFeeStrategy, TaxPolicy — so new promo types obey OCP, and item customizations use Decorator rather than subclass explosion. It makes agent assignment atomic, dedupes order placement idempotently, and handles out-of-stock/offline/promo-invalid at checkout. Senior signal: price snapshotting and the multi-actor state machine.

interviewer_notes: Have them scope single vs multi-restaurant and promo types early. Two differentiators: (1) Cart-vs-Order separation with price snapshotting — if they let Order read live menu prices, hit them with the 'price changed after add-to-cart' case; (2) modeling the lifecycle as a State machine across three actors rather than a status field. Test pricing extensibility with 'add a BOGO promo without editing PricingEngine' and customizations with the Decorator probe. Reserve time for atomic agent assignment. Keep them in object-design territory, not infra.
